inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $1,363M (9M FY2026 10-Q: $1,160M). Disney publishes no combined SBC+withholding-tax figure and does not tag equity-award tax withholdings separately in XBRL (they sit in 'other financing'); the add-back alone is used, which slightly understates the true cost.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 (52-week-normalised estimate; FY2026 ends 3-Oct-2026 and is a 53-week year)
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 27-Jun-2026), 1,743M, from the 10-Q XBRL. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Disney is an active repurchaser ($7.245B in 9M FY2026 against a ~$7B FY2026 target; $3.5B FY2025), so the flat count is funded, and the buybacks are value-neutral here.
inputs.base_revenue_note: 9M FY2026 revenue $76,397M (Q1 25,981 / Q2 25,168 / Q3 25,248, 10-Q XBRL) + Q4 at FY2025 Q4 ($22,464M) x ~1.06 on a 52-week basis = ~$99.3B. The 53rd week (~+$1.7B) is excluded so year-1 (FY2027) growth is not depressed by a calendar artefact.
inputs.margin_anchor_note: The CSV 'EBITDA' (segment OI + total D&A = $22,877M FY2025) double-counts: Disney's total segment operating income excludes corporate/unallocated costs (~$1.45B) and TFCF/Hulu acquisition amortization, while total D&A includes that amortization ($1,467M FY2025). Owner EBITDA rebuilt as segment OI - corporate + depreciation (D&A less acquisition amortization) + SBC add-back. FY2026 52-week estimate: segment OI ~18.6B (9M 14,758 + Q4 ~3.9B at guided ~12% growth) - 1.45B + ~4.25B + 1.56B SBC = ~$23.0B, 23.2% of revenue. da_pct is depreciation only (~4.3%); acquired-intangible amortization is excluded because it is not tax-deductible cash-relevant for a stock-acquired TFCF.
inputs.fcf_anchor_note: FY2025: OCF 18,101 - capex 8,024 = reported FCF 10,077; owner FCF 8,714 after SBC. TTM to Q3 FY2026: OCF 16,989, capex 8,696, FCF 8,293, SBC 1,519, owner FCF 6,774 (capex ramp). FY2026 guidance ~$19B OCF / ~$9B capex implies ~$10B reported, ~$8.4B owner, ~$10B unlevered. Year-1 (FY2027) component build gives ~$10.3B unlevered owner FCF, ~9.9% margin - consistent with the guidance-implied run-rate plus a year of growth.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (interest expense $1.38B 9M FY2026 on ~$46B), after-tax ~3.6%. Market weights ~80/20 (market cap ~$185B vs $46B debt) -> WACC ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent (~$0.66B/yr next twelve months) is inside operating costs and therefore inside EBITDA; the $3.2B operating-lease liability is NOT in net debt. One treatment, applied once. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of ESPN, Fubo, Shanghai and Hong Kong Disneyland). NCI charged once, in the equity bridge at an estimated market value (see equity_bridge), not in the flows. NCI net income: FY2025 $1,027M, 9M FY2026 $506M; NCI book $6,810M at 27-Jun-2026 (up from $4,743M at FY2025, reflecting the NFL 10% ESPN stake and Fubo 30% minority).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route, 10-year horizon) per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company' -- Disney is a diversified operating company (parks/cruises, streaming, linear networks, ESPN, studios), not a bank/REIT/holdco; no prior memory entry, first valuation. US filer, USD flows and quote. Net debt at the latest balance sheet (27-Jun-2026 10-Q): borrowings 46,041 (current 8,627 + non-current 37,414) - cash 5,185 = 40,856. Interest income not stripped: Disney is a net-debt company (investment income $246M FY2025 is mostly equity-method/other, and equity-method income stays inside segment OI, so equity-method investments ($6.3B book) are NOT added to the bridge). Horizon is 10 years because the capex supercycle ($60B Experiences plan over ~10 years) and the streaming margin ramp mean year-5 owner-FCF margin is still below maturity. DATA WARNING: the Metrics.csv/DB quarterly labels for FY2025-FY2026 are shifted one quarter (e.g. 'Q4 2025' = $25,981M is actually Q1 FY2026, quarter ended 27-Dec-2025); this build reads the quarters directly from SEC XBRL with their end dates. Annual rows are correct.

equity_bridge.item: Q4 FY2026 owner FCF generated after the 27-Jun-2026 balance sheet (estimate)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 guidance ~$19B OCF / ~$9B capex less 9M actuals (12,515 / 6,780) implies ~$4.3B Q4 reported FCF, ~$3.9B after SBC; taken at $3.0B for conservatism. Projections start at FY2027, so without this item the quarter would be counted nowhere.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at estimated market value
equity_bridge.note: NCI net income ~$0.75B/yr run-rate (FY2025 1,027; 9M FY2026 506) x ~15x = ~$11B; covers Hearst 20% + NFL 10% of ESPN, Fubo 30%, and the Shanghai/Hong Kong resort partners. Book NCI is $6.8B (27-Jun-2026 10-Q), which understates the ESPN stakes.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, total equity incl. NCI), cross-checked against revenue 3yr CAGR 4.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs are meaningless: FY2020 GAAP EPS was negative (5yr n/a) and FY2025 EPS $6.88 includes a ~$3.3B non-cash deferred tax benefit (effective tax rate -11.9%), inflating the 3yr to 58.5%. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR is n/a because FY2022 owner FCF was ~$0.08B (OCF 6,002 - capex 4,943 - SBC 977); 5yr owner-FCF CAGR 23.2% is off the COVID FY2020 base. Revenue 5yr 7.6% is flattered by the FY2020 COVID trough; the 3yr 4.5% and equity 5.4% are the usable anchors.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2020 3,069; FY2022 82; FY2023 3,754; FY2024 7,193; FY2025 8,714. SBC-adjusted and reported 5yr CAGRs are nearly identical (23.2% vs 22.9%): SBC (~1.4% of revenue) is small for Disney and not growing faster than cash flow.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +5.5% on a 52-week base (guided double-digit adj. EPS growth, Q3 FY2026 revenue +7%), fading to 3% as linear-network decline offsets streaming and Experiences growth.
base.margin_rationale: 23.2% FY2026 anchor rising ~1.8pp to 25% by FY2031 as streaming moves from ~10% to mid-teens margins and new park/cruise capacity opens, partly offset by sports-rights inflation and linear decline.
base.capex_rationale: ~$9B FY2026 guide (~9% of revenue) held through the peak of the $60B Experiences plan, easing to 7% terminal (FY2017-18 steady state 6.6-7.5%). D&A rises from 4.3% to 5.0% as the new capacity depreciates.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 book rate -11.9% was a deferred-tax benefit; cash tax paid FY2023-25 averaged ~$2.1B. Unlevered cash rate 19% ramping to 21% (21% federal + state - FDII).
base.wc_rationale: Zero: deferred revenue (parks prepaid, DTC) roughly offsets growing film/TV production spend running through OCF.

scenario_narratives.base: Streaming holds double-digit margins and drifts to the mid-teens, the Experiences capex program opens capacity roughly on plan with price-led growth offsetting soft domestic attendance, and ESPN DTC scales enough to absorb sports-rights inflation while linear networks decline mid-single digits a year. Revenue grows ~5% fading to 3%, owner EBITDA margin rises ~1.8pp to 25%, and capex stays near 9% of revenue through the peak of the $60B plan before easing to 7%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Streaming reaches Netflix-like high-teens margins with bundling and ad tiers lifting ARPU; ESPN DTC converts cord-cutters at scale; new parks, lands and the 13-ship cruise fleet earn Experiences-level returns; a strong IP slate (post-Zootopia 2/Avatar) keeps the flywheel spinning. Revenue compounds 6-7% early, margin reaches 27.5%, and capex normalises faster as the build program peaks.
scenario_narratives.bear: Linear TV losses accelerate faster than streaming profit grows, NBA/NFL/college rights escalators keep compressing Sports operating income (-17% in Q3 FY2026), domestic park attendance weakness turns into a discretionary-spending downturn just as the $60B capacity comes on, and the new CEO misfires on content strategy. Revenue grows 2-3.5%, margin erodes toward 22%, capex stays elevated, and the terminal is priced at 12x as a no-growth media conglomerate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: the linear-network profit pool is in structural decline, sports-rights costs are contractually escalating, and a first-year CEO is steering a $60B capex commitment into a softening domestic-attendance backdrop. Base 50% as the guided path (double-digit EPS growth FY2026-27, streaming double-digit margins) is on track. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs streaming, ESPN DTC and parks returns to all go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Disney is valued as a single consolidated operating company on owner FCF (SBC expensed, flat diluted share count) over 10 years, because the Experiences capex supercycle and the streaming margin ramp both mature beyond year 5. Terminal value is capped at a mature-media multiple (15x base) rather than left to Gordon, and minority interests (ESPN partners, Fubo, Asian resort partners) are deducted at market value because the flows are consolidated.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity: every 1pp of revenue in sustained capex is ~$1B+ of FCF a year; the $60B Experiences plan could be accelerated further.
Linear networks decline faster than modelled, removing a high-margin profit pool before streaming fully replaces it.
Sports-rights inflation (NBA, NFL, college) outpacing ESPN DTC monetisation.
Terminal multiple: the cap (15x base) binds below Gordon (~17x at 8.5%/2.5%); the sensitivity grid shows the uncapped range.
NCI valuation is an estimate; ESPN's 30% minority stakes could be worth more than ~$11B if ESPN DTC succeeds.
